metadata.source: Digital Corpus of Sanskrit (DCS), text ID 242. http://www.sanskrit-linguistics.org/dcs/ Segmentation follows the DCS line/pāda boundaries; chapter and verse labels are taken from the DCS references.

children.translated_text: Up to the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> and the <s>udayanīya</s>.

children.text: tasyām eva sthālyām aniṣkasitāyāṃ śrapayati tad barhis tan mekṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: He cooks it in that same cooking-pot, without its having been taken out; that is the sacred grass, that is the stirring-spoon.
They perform the rites at the front of the hall.

children.text: teṣv eva deśeṣv agnim ājyabhāgānāṃ prathamaṃ yajati pathyāṃ svastim uttamām ||
children.translated_text: In those very places he first sacrifices to Agni among the portions of ghee, and last to <s>Pathyā Svasti</s>.
Those which are the sacrificial formulas of the <s>prāyaṇīya</s> have been stated.
He immolates a barren cow belonging to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s> as the <s>anūbandhyā</s> victim.
The procedure for it is like that of the regular animal sacrifice.

children.text: mitrāvaruṇābhyāṃ gor vapāyā medaso 'nubrūhi mitrāvaruṇābhyāṃ gor vapāyā medasaḥ preṣyeti saṃpraiṣau ||
children.translated_text: The two directions are: 'Recite for <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, for the omentum and fat of the cow'; and 'For <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, for the omentum and fat of the cow, give the command.'
In the same way, in the cut portions, he changes the ending to 'of the oblation'.
Some hand down three <s>anūbandhyā</s> victims.
Namely, one for <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, one for the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s>, and one for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: dvirūpā maitrāvaruṇī bahurūpā vaiśvadevī rohiṇī bārhaspatyā ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Maitrāvaruṇī</s> cow is two-colored, the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> many-colored, and the <s>Bārhaspatyā</s> red.
They proceed silently with the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> in the middle.

children.text: tā na sarvatrālabheta vājapeye rājasūye sattre sahasre sarvavedase vā ||
children.translated_text: He should not immolate them everywhere, but at the <s>Vājapeya</s>, the <s>Rājasūya</s>, a sattra, a rite of a thousand, or a <s>sarvavedasa</s>.

children.text: yaḥ kāmayeta sarvo me yajñaḥ syāt sarasa iti sa etās tisro 'nūbandhyā ālabheta ||
children.translated_text: Whoever should desire, 'May my whole sacrifice be full of sap,' should immolate these three <s>anūbandhyā</s> victims.

children.text: anūbandhyāvapāyāṃ hutāyāṃ dakṣiṇe vedyante yajamānaḥ keśaśmaśru vāpayate ||
children.translated_text: When the omentum of the <s>anūbandhyā</s> has been offered, at the southern end of the altar the sacrificer has his hair and beard shaved.
The animal-cake of the <s>anūbandhyā</s> follows.

children.text: ayaṃ puro bhuva iti pañcāśataṃ prāṇabhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: With 'This in front is the earth,' he places fifty life-bearing bricks,
ten in each direction, ten crosswise,
placing an inner one in the middle and then each outer one.

children.text: prācī diśām iti pañcāśatam apānabhṛto yathā prāṇabhṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: With 'The eastern one of the directions,' he places fifty breath-bearing bricks in the same way as the life-bearing ones,
placing an outer one and then each inner one.
'From life extend breath;
from breath extend down-breath;
from down-breath extend diffused breath;
from diffused breath extend sight;
from sight extend hearing;
from hearing extend mind;
from mind extend speech;
from speech extend the self;
from the self extend the earth;
from the earth extend the mid-space;
from the mid-space extend heaven;

children.text: divaḥ suvaḥ saṃtanv iti dvādaśa saṃtatīḥ ||
children.translated_text: from heaven extend the <s>suvar</s> world': these are the twelve continuities.

children.text: pṛthivī vaśāmāvāsyā garbho vanaspatayo jarāyv agnir vatso 'gnihotraṃ pīyūṣaḥ
children.translated_text: 'Earth is a barren cow; the new-moon night is the embryo; the forest trees are the afterbirth; Agni is the calf; the Agnihotra is the milk,

children.text: antarikṣaṃ vaśā dhātā garbho rudro jarāyu vāyur vatso gharmaḥ pīyūṣaḥ
children.translated_text: the mid-space is a barren cow; Dhātṛ is the embryo; Rudra is the afterbirth; Vāyu is the calf; the Gharma is the milk,

children.text: dyaur vaśā stanayitnur garbho nakṣatrāṇi jarāyu sūryo vatso vṛṣṭiḥ pīyūṣaḥ
children.translated_text: heaven is a barren cow; thunder is the embryo; the stars are the afterbirth; the sun is the calf; rain is the milk,

children.text: ṛg vaśā bṛhadrathaṃtare garbhaḥ praiṣanivido jarāyu yajño vatso dakṣiṇāḥ pīyūṣaḥ
children.translated_text: the Ṛg is a barren cow; the Bṛhat and Rathantara are the embryo; the summonses and invitatory formulas are the afterbirth; the sacrifice is the calf; the priestly gifts are the milk,

children.text: viḍ vaśā rājanyo garbhaḥ paśavo jarāyu rājā vatso baliḥ pīyūṣa iti pañca vaśāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the people are a barren cow; the royal man is the embryo; the animals are the afterbirth; the king is the calf; tribute is the milk': these are the five barren cows.

children.text: artheta sthādhvagato 'gnir vas tejiṣṭhena tejasā devatābhir gṛhṇāmīti kumbhaṃ kumbhīṃ cādbhiḥ pūrayitvā śarma ca stha varma ca stha devasya vaḥ savituḥ prasave madhumatīḥ sādayāmīti purastād anusītam upadhāya jyotiṣe vām iti hiraṇyaśalkau pratyasyati ||
children.translated_text: With 'You are for gain; standing on the road, Agni grasps you with the most blazing splendor, with the deities,' he fills a pot and a jar with water; with 'You are shelter and you are armor; at the impulse of the god Savitṛ I set you down, honey-sweet,' he places them before the line; with 'For light, you two,' he throws in two flakes of gold.

children.text: evam uttarā uttarair mantraiḥ pratidiśam anusītam
children.translated_text: In the same way, one after another, with the following mantras, he places them in each direction,
four in the middle.

children.text: śukrā stha vīryāvatīr indrasya va indriyāvato devatābhir gṛhṇāmi ||
children.translated_text: 'You are bright, rich in heroic power; I grasp you, belonging to Indra who possesses power, with the deities.'

children.text: yo rudro agnāv iti raudraṃ gāvīdhukaṃ carum ||
children.translated_text: With 'That Rudra who is in the fire,' he prepares the Rudra-related gruel of gavedhukā grain.

children.text: etena yajuṣā yasyām iṣṭakāyāṃ śatarudrīyaṃ juhoti tasyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati ||
children.translated_text: With this yajus he sets it on the brick on which he offers the Śatarudrīya.

children.text: tisṛdhanvam ayācitaṃ yajamāno brāhmaṇāya dattvā yat te rudra puro dhanur ity etair yathāliṅgam upatiṣṭhate ||
children.translated_text: After the sacrificer has given an unasked-for three-bow gift to a brahmin, he worships with the formulas beginning 'Your bow, O Rudra, in front,' according to their indications.

children.text: udakumbham ādāyādhvaryur aśmann ūrjam iti triḥ pradakṣiṇam agniṃ pariṣiñcan paryeti ||
children.translated_text: Taking a water-pot, the adhvaryu goes around the fire three times clockwise, sprinkling it with 'O stone, strength.'

children.text: nidhāya kumbham aśmaṃs te kṣud amuṃ te śug ṛcchatu yaṃ dviṣma iti trir apariṣiñcan pratiparyeti ||
children.translated_text: Setting down the pot, he goes back around it three times in the opposite direction without sprinkling, saying, 'O stone, may your hunger, may your burning heat reach that man whom we hate.'

children.text: yady abhicared idam aham amuṣyāmuṣyāyaṇasyāyuḥ prakṣiṇomīti dakṣiṇasyām uttarasyāṃ vā sraktyāṃ kumbhaṃ prakṣiṇuyāt ||
children.translated_text: If he were to perform hostile magic, he should smash the pot on the southern or northern corner, saying, 'Here I cut off the life of so-and-so, the descendant of so-and-so.'

children.text: avakā vetasaśākhāṃ maṇḍūkaṃ ca dīrghavaṃśe prabadhya samudrasya tvāvakayeti saptabhir aṣṭābhir vāgniṃ vikarṣati ||
children.translated_text: Having fastened avakā grass, a branch of reed, and a frog to a long bamboo, he drags the fire away with seven or eight formulas beginning 'With the avakā of the sea I take you.'

children.text: vikarṣann evānugamayitvā maṇḍūkasya prāṇān sarvān saṃlobhyotkara udasyati ||
children.translated_text: While dragging it away he leads it onward, and after confusing all the breaths of the frog, he throws it on the refuse heap.
He should touch with these any man whom he hates.

children.text: pṛṣṭhair upatiṣṭhate gāyatreṇa purastāt bṛhadrathaṃtarābhyāṃ pakṣau ṛtusthāyajñāyajñiyena puccham dakṣiṇasyāṃ śroṇyāṃ vāravantīyena uttarasyāṃ vāmadevyena ||
children.translated_text: He worships with the back chants: with the Gāyatra in front, with the Bṛhat and Rathantara on the two wings, with the Ṛtusthā and Yajñāyajñiya as the tail, with the Vāravantīya on the right hip, and with the Vāmadevya on the left.
On the near wing he sings the Sāman-verse of Prajāpati.
With 'Father Mātariśvan,' the hotṛ recites the formula belonging to the built-up ukthya.

children.text: hotary akāmayamāne 'dhvaryuḥ stutaśastrayor dohe yajamānaṃ vācayati ||
children.translated_text: When the hotṛ does not desire to do so, at the milking of the chant and recitation the adhvaryu makes the sacrificer recite.

children.text: stutasya stutam asīty atra pravargyam udvāsayati ||
children.translated_text: At the words 'You are the praise of the praised,' he removes the <s>pravargya</s>.
With 'You are Mitra,' the sacrificer brings forward his right arm,
with 'You are Varuṇa,' his left.
Or this may be reversed.

children.text: sam ahaṃ viśvair devair iti vaiśvadevyām āmikṣāyāṃ hastāv upāvaharate ||
children.translated_text: With 'Together am I with all the gods,' he brings forward his hands at the <s>Vaiśvadevī</s> curd-mixture.

children.text: sad asi san me bhūyā iti vā maitrāvaruṇīm āmikṣām eke samāmananti ||
children.translated_text: Some hand down the <s>Maitrāvaruṇī</s> curd-mixture instead, with 'You are being; may there be being for me.'

children.text: agreṇāgnīdhraṃ caturapasrāvaṃ vimitaṃ viminvanti purastādunnataṃ paścānninatam ||
children.translated_text: In front of the Āgnīdhra they measure out a structure with four run-off channels, raised in the east and lowered in the west.

children.text: syonāsi suṣadeti tasmin khādirīm āsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpya kṣatrasya nābhir asīti tasyāṃ kṛttyadhīvāsam āstīryāvanahani viśi mā dṛṃhety avanahyati ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "You are pleasant; you are easy to sit upon," he sets upon it a khadira-wood seat; saying, "You are the navel of royal power," he spreads on it a covering made of hide, and saying, "Do not make me firm in the non-striker, but in the people," he fastens it down.

children.text: syonām ā sīda suṣadām ā sīdeti tām āsādya yajamāno mā tvā hiṃsīn mā mā hiṃsīd ity upaviśati ||
children.translated_text: Having approached it with, "Sit down upon the pleasant one, sit down upon the easy seat," the sacrificer sits, saying, "May you not injure me; may I not injure you."
When he is seated, he addresses him with the formula, "He has sat down, holding firm to the vow."

children.text: tam ṛtvijo ratninaś ca sarvataḥ paryupaviśanti
children.translated_text: The priests and the <s>ratnins</s> sit around him on all sides.
The <s>adhvaryu</s> sits in front.
The <s>brahman</s> sits to the south.
The <s>hotṛ</s> sits behind.
The <s>udgātṛ</s> sits to the north.
When they have sat down, the king addresses the <s>adhvaryu</s>, saying, "O <s>brahman</s>."
The other replies, "You, O king, are the <s>brahman</s>."
In the same way he addresses the <s>brahman</s>, the <s>hotṛ</s>, and the <s>udgātṛ</s>.
The others reply with each successive mantra.

children.text: indrasya vajro 'sīti sphyaṃ brahmā rājñe prayacchati
children.translated_text: Saying, "You are <s>Indra</s>'s thunderbolt," the <s>brahman</s> hands the wooden sword to the king.
The king hands it to the appointed one, the appointed one to the <s>purohita</s>.
The <s>purohita</s> hands it to the <s>ratnins</s>.
They pass it on from the nearer to the farther one.
At the end, it goes to the keeper of the dice.
With it the keeper of the dice should clear out the gaming place, sprinkle it, and cast down the dice.
They are golden, more than a hundred or more than a thousand in number.

children.text: brāhmaṇarājanyavaiśyaśūdrāś catvāras tadyogāḥ paṣṭhauhīṃ vidīvyanta odanam udbruvate ||
children.translated_text: Four men, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>rājanya</s>, a <s>vaiśya</s>, and a <s>śūdra</s>, equipped for that, play for a sterile cow and call out rice.

children.text: tad etasya karmaṇaḥ pūrvāv agnivāhau dakṣiṇā ||
children.translated_text: For this rite, the two oxen that first draw the fire are the sacrificial fee.
They are to be given to the <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: audbhidyaṃ rājña iti tebhyaś catuḥśatān sauvarṇān akṣān udupya vijitya diśo 'bhy ayaṃ rājābhūd iti pañcākṣān rājñe prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: Saying, "The king's Audbhidya," he draws out four hundred golden dice from them, wins the directions, and gives five dice to the king with, "This king has become lord over the directions."
The king calls one whose name is auspicious.
With "O fair-famed one," he calls the charioteer.
With "O very auspicious one," he calls the distributor of shares.
With "O true king," he calls the chamberlain.
Having summoned them, he gives a four-footed field to the <s>brahman</s>.
They become overseers.
Or here he may offer the two oblations that interweave the names.
He has the story of <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> recited.
The verses, mixed with gāthās, are more than a hundred or more than a thousand.
Seated on a golden cushion, the <s>hotṛ</s> recites them.
Standing on golden seats of kuśa grass, the <s>adhvaryu</s> responds.
"Om" is the response to a ṛc verse.
"So be it" is the response to a gāthā.
When the <s>Śunaḥśepa</s> recitation is finished, he gives the golden cushion to the <s>hotṛ</s>.
He gives the golden kuśa-seats to the <s>adhvaryu</s>.
And he gives the two gold plates used for the consecration.
Here he proceeds with the offering to the <s>Maruts</s> and the offering to the <s>Viśve Devāḥ</s>.
But the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> and the <s>iḍā</s> are the same as before.

children.text: upahūtāyām iḍāyām unmucya maṇīn brahmaṇe dadāti ||
children.translated_text: When the <s>iḍā</s> has been called, he unties the jewels and gives them to the <s>brahman</s>.

children.text: ṛṣabhe goṣu jīrṇe yūnaḥ karṇam ājapet piśaṅgarūpas tan nas turīpam ity etābhyām ||
children.translated_text: When a bull has grown old among the cows, he should whisper into the ear of a young one with these two formulas, "Of tawny form," and "That most excellent share for us."

children.text: athainaṃ goṣv apisṛjaty etaṃ yuvānam iti ||
children.translated_text: Then he lets it loose among the cows with, "This young one."

children.text: atha jīrṇam ālabhate prājāpatyam aindraṃ tvāṣṭraṃ vā ||
children.translated_text: Then he takes hold of the old one as an offering to <s>Prajāpati</s>, to <s>Indra</s>, or to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>.
At the preliminary handling he continues with, "Homage to greatness."
With the third verse he offers the omentum.
With the fourth he offers the oblation.
With the fifth he offers what belongs to the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>.
Having set out an eight-dish cake for <s>Agni</s>, he takes hold of a sterile she-goat.

children.text: vāyavyām ālabheta bhūtikāma ity uktāni daivatāni ||
children.translated_text: "One desiring prosperity should take hold of one belonging to <s>Vāyu</s>": the deities have been stated.

children.text: vāyavyayopākaroty ā vāyo bhūṣa śucipā iti ||
children.translated_text: He performs the preliminary handling with the Vāyu formula, "Come, O <s>Vāyu</s>, adorn yourself, O pure-drinking one."

children.text: ākūtyai tvā kāmāya tveti paryagnau kriyamāṇe juhoti ||
children.translated_text: When the fire is being carried around it, he offers with, "For intention I take you; for desire I take you."

children.text: tvaṃ turīyā vaśinī vaśāsīty udīcīṃ nīyamānām anumantrayate ||
children.translated_text: As it is being led northward, he addresses it with, "You are the fourth, the ruling sterile cow."
As it is being killed, he addresses it with, "You are a she-goat, richest in wealth."
With "Stretching the thread," he offers the omentum.

children.text: anulbaṇaṃ vayata joguvām apa iti haviḥ ||
children.translated_text: With "Weave without knots; drive away the Joguvā," he offers the oblation.
With "You are the oblation of the mind," they eat the remains of the oblation.

children.text: sā vā eṣā trayāṇām evāvaruddhety uktam ||
children.translated_text: It has been stated that this one is secured for only three persons.

children.text: tasyai vā etasyā ekam evādevayajanaṃ yad ālabdhāyām abhro bhavati ||
children.translated_text: For this animal there is only one case in which the sacrifice is not made to the gods: when, after it has been taken hold of, there is a cloud.

children.text: yad ālabdhāyām abhraḥ syād apsu vā praveśayet sarvāṃ vā yajamāna evānvahaṃ prāśnīyāt ||
children.translated_text: If there should be a cloud after it has been taken hold of, he should either make the whole animal enter the waters, or the sacrificer himself should eat it day by day.
The Jayā, Abhyātāna, and Rāṣṭrabhṛt formulas have been explained in the Brāhmaṇa.
Among the Abhyātānas he appends the formula beginning, "In this, O <s>brahman</s>."

children.text: yena karmaṇertset tatra hotavyā ṛdhnoty eva tena karmaṇeti vijñāyate ||
children.translated_text: With whatever rite he should desire to prosper, there the oblation should be offered; it is understood that by that very rite he prospers.
